fullPassage:
Resilience: Recovering from Difficult Times

Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges, both big and small. So why can some people handle tough times and become stronger while others remain unchanged and helpless? The answer lies in resilience — the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties.

The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly normal to feel down every now and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them.

Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. In simple terms, resilience is not about being emotionless: Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall. But you keep going. It is like working out to build your muscles; it takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.

det.tip: working out(운동)과 muscles(근육)가 나오는 문장 전체를 그대로 옮겨 쓰면 됩니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: '~에 노출되다(be exposed to)'가 되도록 expose를 변형.
det.analysis: 구문 분석: need to be + 과거분사(p.p.) 형태의 수동태 구조로, 사람은 세균에 '노출되는' 대상이므로 be exposed to(~에 노출되다)가 되어야 한다. 따라서 expose의 과거분사형 exposed가 옳다.
det.tip: 노출되는 대상이므로 수동태 be + p.p.(be exposed)를 씁니다. expose → exposed.

questions.passage:
Resilience: Recovering from Difficult Times

Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges, both big and small.  So why can some people handle tough times and become stronger while others remain unchanged and helpless?  The answer lies in resilience — the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties. 

The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill.  However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly normal to feel down every now and then.  Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them. 

Think of it like building your body's immune system.  Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience.  In simple terms, resilience is not about being emotionless: Resilience means you experience.  You feel.  You fail.  You hurt.  You fall.  But you keep going.  It is like working out to build your muscles; it takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.

det.tip: 요지는 글쓴이의 핵심 주장입니다. 회복탄력성은 '기를 수 있는' 능력이라는 점에 주목하세요.

questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'회복탄력성은 문제를 예방하지는 못하지만, 여러분이 그것에 맞서 극복하도록 도와줄 것이다.'

[조건]
(1) and, but, face, help, it, not, overcome, prevent, problems, resilience, them, will, will, you를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 14단어로 쓸 것

det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- Resilience will not prevent problems(회복탄력성은 문제를 예방하지 못할 것이다): 조동사 will + not + 동사원형 prevent
- but it will help you face and overcome them(하지만 그것에 맞서 극복하도록 도와줄 것이다): help + 목적어(you) + 동사원형(face and overcome), them = problems
- 'not A but B'의 대조 구조로 두 절이 연결된다
det.tip: help + 목적어 + 동사원형(help you face and overcome). them은 앞의 problems를 가리킵니다.

questions.wa: Resilience will not prevent problems but it will help you face and overcome them
accept: Resilience will not prevent problems but it will help you face and overcome them
